title: Acceptance timeline and clearance pathway for cross-team PRD sign-offs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: coordinate a deterministic acceptance timeline and handoff path for the Console PRD introducing multi-tenant routing policies and canary rollout controls. This ticket captures dependencies, reviewers, explicit acceptance criteria per discipline (Engineering, Design, Legal), and a contingency rollforward plan to avoid blocking the 2026.04 runtime release window.
background: PM wrote initial PRD on 2026-02-10. Early design mockups were posted in Figma. Engineering requested clarifications around API contract and rollout semantics on 2026-02-15. Legal flagged data residency and audit retention language on 2026-02-18. Several cross-team comments are unresolved and are blocking final sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering: API spec (OpenAPI) updated and merged with exact request/response examples; integration tests demonstrating canary fallback in staging; benchmark micro-SLOs validated (p90 < 120ms for control path).
Design: Figma flows for canary UX and error states reviewed and approved; accessibility checklist completed for the new modal and alerts.
Legal: Data residency & retention language approved; audit log schema and KMS handling documented and legal attestation present.
Cross-team: A single merged PRD version exists in Confluence with an approval stamp from PM, Eng (tech lead), Design lead, and Legal counsel.
Deployment gating: Canary rollout plan with metrics and automatic rollback thresholds documented and included in release playbook.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after last sync. Requesting owners from Eng/Design/Legal to triage ambiguity in 'route affinity' section.
2026-02-22 - Liam Nguyen (ENG): Raised two API contract questions (query params vs body) and noted potential perf impact for long-lived KV cache entries. Assigned ENG-2191 to track change set.
2026-02-24 - Sofia Martinez (DES): Uploaded updated flows in Figma addressing edge case modals. Requested clarity on error copy — deferred to PM for tone.

2026-02-27 - Nathan Chen (LEGAL): Flagged retention phrase 'until customer deletes' as insufficient; requested explicit retention TTLs and KMS usage details. Legal review scoped to epoch-based retention policy.
2026-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Compiled combined diffs into Confluence. Marked sections that require sign-off with comment tags. Added provisional acceptance dates to timeline.
2026-03-06 - Liam Nguyen (ENG): Completed draft OpenAPI and staged integration tests; posted benchmark results for control path (p50/p90). Linking GH PR for review.
2026-03-08 - Sofia Martinez (DES): Confirmed accessibility checklist completed (WCAG AA) and left Figma comments cleared.
2026-03-10 - Nathan Chen (LEGAL): Provided attestation note and requested one minor wording change in PRD section 4.2. Change committed by PM. Legal now marks "needs final review".
decisions: Use query param 'canary_percent' as primary toggle for rollout and keep body-based overrides for advanced clients.
Adopt epoch-based retention with a default 90-day audit log TTL; customers can request longer retention via Enterprise contract.
Design pattern: show non-blocking toast for canary mismatches and preserve primary route affinity in UI.
next_steps: PM to incorporate Legal wording change into Confluence PRD (due 2026-03-11).
Eng to merge OpenAPI spec and link to integration tests (due 2026-03-13).
Design to attach final annotated Figma frames and copy (due 2026-03-12).
Cross-team sign-off meeting scheduled 2026-03-14; bring runbook and rollout metrics dashboard.
notes: If any reviewer cannot sign off by due_date, fallback plan: ship limited-surface canary with manual gating and postpone full rollout to next cycle. Track decisions in the release playbook.
